records.title: Binance Hack: $6.3B Drained on 9 Chains, $2.7B Frozen
records.summary: Bitquery's article states that each wallet drained in the October 29 incident carries a Binance proof-of-reserves label in Bitquery's address data (lines 61–66); it then identifies five Binance accounts on XRPL sending approximately 233.5M XRP (lines 69–76). At 06:43 UTC on October 30, the XRP receiver still held 233.5M XRP and had never sent a transaction; Bitquery found no transfer to a known exchange, mixer or bridge at that cutoff (lines 144–170). The same investigation reports Circle froze 823M USDC in the main Ethereum receiver at 21:04 UTC, Tether froze USDT, some stolen USDT was used as Aave collateral for an ETH loan, and Ripple was among issuers freezing tokens whose exact identities are not specified (lines 90–132). Bitquery explicitly says the XRP and Solana drains share no address with the other chain clusters and are linked by timing, transaction construction and Binance's aggregate (lines 190–200).
records.limitations: The PoR designation is Bitquery's address-data label, not a raw official Binance XRP export independently matched in this run. Bitquery warns wallet labels may be incomplete. The 06:43 UTC receiver balance is a historical cutoff, not current. Circle's freeze is USDC on Ethereum, not an XRP or XRPL freeze. The Aave collateral is stolen USDT and the loan asset is ETH; amount and market impact are not specified. Ripple's frozen token identity is not specified; do not infer RLUSD or XRP. XRP/Solana share no address with other chain clusters, so common-actor attribution remains qualified.
